claims.text: Replacing EAM reference potentials with an ab initio-trained ML interatomic potential will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in high-entropy alloys near melting.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states near their melting temperatures.
The relevant high-entropy alloys are typically equiatomic or near-equiatomic.
The ML-IP should be trained on an extensive ab initio dataset spanning diverse solid and liquid configurations.
The proposed method applies at temperatures near or above 0.9 times the melting temperature.
The proposed method applies across equiatomic and near-equiatomic HEA composition ranges.
Flexible ML-IP functional forms can represent many-body interactions and adapt to varying local atomic environments.
Learning diverse bonding environments and many-body effects from ab initio data will make ML-IP sampling more closely match the ab initio target distribution.
An ML-IP reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration errors relative to TOR-TILD EAM references.
ML-IP-based free-energy estimates will agree more closely with ab initio benchmarks than estimates obtained using TOR-TILD EAM references.
TOR-TILD currently uses fixed EAM reference potentials.
Fixed EAM references inadequately cover the configurational diversity of ab initio HEA liquid states.
The intervention may have limited applicability under extreme compositional heterogeneity or far-from-equilibrium conditions.
The quantitative reduction in thermodynamic-integration mismatch cannot be specified until direct benchmarking against ab initio molecular-dynamics data.
A controlled comparison of ML-IP and EAM reference paths can measure free-energy differences, phase-space overlap, and path mismatch.
Failure of the ML-IP path to significantly reduce mismatch or move free-energy predictions closer to the ab initio benchmark would falsify the hypothesis.
